source_review.notes: Reviewed Lehman-Yao's primary concurrency paper, Bayer-McCreight's original page-tree paper, CMU B+ notes, current PostgreSQL B-tree and nbtree maintainer documentation, and current SQLite format, module, and architecture documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product-specific behavior is presented as implementation evidence, not a universal B+ definition.

evidence: Checked composite entry identity, separator arrays, child gaps, leaf links, fences, fan-out, leaf capacity, height, and result size notation.
Checked right-lower-bound equality and half-open child intervals are used consistently in prose and model.
Checked logical entries, copied routing separators, page visits, physical reads, heap probes, and transaction visibility remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Classic B-tree promotion and B+ leaf-copy semantics are explicitly separated.

evidence: Recomputed model splits at capacity three: leaves 5,6,7 | 10,12,17 | 20,30 and separators 10,20.
Recomputed inclusive range 6 through 20 as 6,7,10,12,17,20 across all three leaves.
Recomputed Exercise 2: final leaves 8,9 | 10,11 | 15,17,20, root separators 10,15, and range 9 through 17 as 9,10,11,15,17.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite count-capacity arithmetic does not establish byte occupancy or production fan-out.

evidence: Verified lower-bound separators route equality right and copied boundary entries remain authoritative at leaves.
Verified point lookup follows one height path and ideal range cost adds leaf pages proportional to output under stated occupancy assumptions.
Verified routing correctness plus leaf-chain equivalence and endpoint filtering yields ordered range completeness in the sequential model.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Concurrent range correctness additionally requires the stated fence, version, snapshot, and lifetime protocol.

evidence: Reviewed empty/single leaf, exact boundary equality, root/internal/leaf split, delete-first-key, redistribution, merge, root contraction, and reverse/resume endpoints.
Reviewed duplicates, collation changes, truncated separators, posting/overflow, maximum encodings, corrupt links/fences/ranges, cycles, omission, and duplicate leaf ownership.
Reviewed split/scan races, unpinned/recycled pages, version wrap, deadlock, stale parent routing, crash prefixes, allocator leaks, torn writes, snapshot expiry, and verifier consistency.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes deletion, bytes, concurrency, recovery, duplicates, and MVCC; these remain separately assigned evidence obligations.

evidence: The model checks nonempty bounded leaves, strict local order, exact separators as right-leaf minima, adjacent forward links, terminal null, and globally sorted chain.
Leaf split partitions every entry once, keeps the copied separator in the right leaf, and rebuilds routing and links deterministically.
Exact output checks root separators, leaves, copied-boundary presence, height, two lookups, range result, chain order, and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: The model intentionally has one internal root and assumes exclusive atomic mutation.

evidence: Reviewed routing induction from total order, separator intervals, child ranges, leaf split copying, internal propagation, and root growth.
Reviewed range argument from lower-bound seek through internally ordered leaves, exact chain topology, endpoint/visibility filtering, and resume identity.
Reviewed durable refinement across page validation, link/fence publication, parent/root/allocation WAL, page generations, recovery, and independent topology audit.
proof_review.notes: These are scoped proof structures and obligations, not a mechanized verification of an implementation.

evidence: Routing, range, and durability arguments are separately labeled with their assumptions.
The Lehman-Yao right-link idea is described as a full protocol requirement, not permission to add an unvalidated next pointer.
Finite model, current product formats, source reachability, testing prescriptions, and benchmarks are not generalized into proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Transaction isolation is explicitly separated from physical page latching.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It reproduced two leaf splits, separator copies, forward-chain order, successful 17, absent 15, exact inclusive range, and valid=True.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local structure/link checks passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No page codec, real I/O, internal split, deletion, duplicates, concurrent scan, MVCC, WAL, crash recovery, fuzzing, migration, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter makes leaf-only authority, separator-copy semantics, right-lower-bound routing, leaf topology, output-sensitive scans, and the separation of structural latches from transaction isolation precise.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed payload/locator choices, duplicates/posting lists, separator truncation, links/fences, cursor resume, page parsing, concurrency/reclamation, structural recovery, topology audit, migration, observability, and correctness-first benchmarks.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review contrasts B and B+ directly; the executable model exposes copied separators and linked range traversal; ten examples cover semantic, concurrency, recovery, and performance boundaries; five exercises include complete designs and audit answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Lehman, Yao, Bayer, McCreight, CMU, PostgreSQL, SQLite, database, concurrency, storage-engine, formal-methods, security, reliability, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a variable-byte page format, internal split/deletion, duplicate/posting implementation, concurrent tree or scan, MVCC/isolation, reclamation, WAL/recovery, corruption repair, migration, production performance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
